headline: Authors report frequent context compaction preserves performance across tested long-horizon and long-input tasks
summary: In arXiv:2611.05306v1, the authors evaluate context compaction and selective input reading on six long-horizon and seven long-input benchmark families. For end-of-conversation compaction, they report broadly near-baseline accuracy across tested thresholds for Claude Opus 4.5 and GPT 5.6 Sol, alongside estimated optimized retail-cost reductions; the estimates are not observed invoice savings. In a single-action-compaction condition, median live context is 7–9K tokens and maximum context 15–37K, while GPT 5.6 Sol falls 2.0 and 3.3 percentage points below its baselines on two coding benchmarks. These are author-reported results from the tested benchmarks and models; independent reproduction and universal transfer are not established.
